title: Engineering 3D Cellularized Collagen Gels for Vascular Tissue Regeneration
protocol: Prepare 50 ml centrifuge tubes as a culture medium reservoir.
Drill two 5 mm diameter holes, one at 20 mm from the bottom and another at 20 mm from the top of the reservoir.
Insert two luer fittings into 5 mm length silicone tubes.
Press-fit these luer fittings through the drilled holes in the reservoir.
Seal all connections with medical grade silicone glue.
Insert a 0.22 µm filter into the upper port of the reservoir.
Insert a luer septum into the lower port of the reservoir.
Drill a 4.5 mm diameter hole at the center of the ventilated cap of the reservoir tube without damaging the aerating holes.
Prepare a stir bar (diameter = 4.5 mm, length = 100 mm) as a mandrel for the construct.
Prepare two silicone conical stoppers (length = 10 mm, middle hole diameter = 4.5 mm).
Press-fit the mandrel into the hole in the cap.
Insert the two stoppers over the mandrel so that the cap is fitted between them.
Adjust the position of the mandrel to ensure its useful length is 78 mm.
Apply a primer and then medical grade silicone glue to the surfaces that will be in contact before joining the cap and the silicone conical stoppers together.
Remove excess glue on the cap.
Let it dry at room temperature for 1-3 days.
Prepare 3 silicone tubes with specified dimensions.
Cut tube 1 longitudinally and open it over tube 2.
Stick together tubes 1 and 2 using silicone glue.
Cut sterile surgical gauze to a size of 5 cm x 7 cm.
Roll the gauze tightly around tube 3 along its longest side.
Insert the tube 1-tube 2 complex over the rolled gauze.
Add silicone glue to secure together the gauze, tubes 1 and 2, and tube 3.
Cut the gauze at a length of 8 mm.
Assemble the mandrel-cap complex as described in Figure 2.
Coat the mandrel with medical grade grease (Figure 2A).
Place the gauze-grips over the coated mandrel (Figure 2B).
Distance the grips at fixed value of 35 mm from each other.
Prepare a tubular mold by removing the bottom part of a 10 ml syringe to final length of 8 mm (Figure 2B).
Insert the mold over the gauze grips-equipped mandrel-cap assembly (housing-mold complex), snap-fitting it onto the silicone stopper (Figure 2C).
Hold the silicone stopper tightly when inserting the mold.
Autoclave the reservoir and the housing-mold complex.

Expand porcine aortic smooth muscle cells in 175 cm² culture flasks with complete culture medium consisting of Dulbecco’s Modified Eagle Medium, 10% porcine serum, 10% fetal bovine serum, and 1% penicillin-streptomycin.
At approximately 90% confluence, detach pSMCs by removing the culture medium from the flask.
Add 5 ml of trypsin solution to the flask and incubate for 10 min at 37 °C with 5% CO₂ and 100% humidity.
Resuspend the detached cells in complete culture medium at a concentration of 4 x 10⁶ cells/ml.
Extract collagen bundles from rat-tail tendons in PBS solution.
Transfer collagen fibers to acetone for 5 min, then to isopropanol (70%) for another 5 min.
Immerse the fibers in acetic acid (0.02 N) at 4 °C for 48 hours.
Blend and freeze the viscous solution at -20 °C for 3 days.
Lyophilize the frozen solution to obtain collagen sponges.
Solubilize collagen sponges into an acetic acid solution (0.02 N, concentration of 4 g/L) and centrifuge at 29,581 g force for 45 min.
Sterilize the collagen solution through dialysis against acetic acid (0.02 N, 1 hour), chloroform 1% (v/v, 1 hour), and sterile acetic acid (0.02 N) with daily changes for one week.
Collect the sterile collagen solution in a sterile cell culture hood at a concentration of 4 g/L.
Prepare 50 ml of sterile buffer solution by mixing 35 ml of DMEM (5x), 4 ml of HEPES (1 N), and 3 ml of NaOH (1 N) in 8 ml of sterile deionized water.
Mix 50% (v/v) of sterile collagen solution with 25% (v/v) of buffer solution and 25% (v/v) of pSMCs suspension in complete culture medium.
Measure the pH of the mixture and ensure it is between 7.0 and 7.4.
Pour gently 9 ml of cells-and-collagen mixture into the housing/mold complex.
Let the mixture gel at room temperature for 1 hour under a cell culture hood.
Remove the mold and transfer carefully the construct into the reservoir containing 35 ml of culture medium.
Incubate the construct vertically in an incubator (T = 37 °C, 5% CO2, 100% humidity) for 1 or 2 weeks.
Change the culture medium every 2 days by aspirating old medium and refilling with fresh culture medium.
Place the scanning laser interferometer in the cell culture hood.
Flip the interferometer from vertical to horizontal using a spirit level.
Transfer the bioreactor into the cell culture hood.
Remove the construct from the reservoir of the bioreactor.
Mount the construct on the mandrel and place it in the pathway of the laser beam.
Position the construct orthogonally with respect to the beam axis.
Read the value displayed on the screen, corresponding to the external diameter of the construct.
Calculate the wall thickness based on the external and internal diameters.
Repeat steps 2.3.1 to 2.3.5 every hour for the first 12 hours.
Then repeat these steps every 24 hours thereafter.
Sample 1 ml of old culture medium when changing the medium.
Measure lactate and glucose concentrations with a blood gas analyzer using the sampled medium.
Use 1 ml of fresh culture medium as baseline for glucose and lactate concentration measurements.
Repeat steps 2.3.6 and 2.3.7 every two days after medium changes.
Transfer the static bioreactor into the cell culture hood after one or two weeks of maturation period.
Transfer gently the mature construct from its mandrel to a Petri dish containing 40 ml of fresh culture medium.
Install the experimental set-up consisting of a micromechanical tester with a 5 or 10 N load cell and a bath containing PBS at 37 °C.
Balance the load cell and extensometer by resetting both measurements while no sample is mounted onto the machine.
Mount the tubular construct onto in-house-built gripping devices for longitudinal testing.
Connect the gripping devices to the load cell and the base of the PBS bath.
Wrap the gripping devices and gauze grips with Teflon tape to prevent slipping during the test.
Mount the sample onto the micromechanical tester.
Mount the tubular construct onto a plastic pipe marked with 5 mm gaps.
Cut 10 mm rings from the tubular construct.
Measure the length of the ring-shaped specimen using a vernier caliper.
Mount the ring-shaped specimen at the center of two stainless steel bars on the micromechanical tester.
Stretch the construct to its initial gauge length.
Maintain the construct in this position for 10 min in a pseudo-physiological environment.
Apply 10% cyclic strain of the initial gauge length (30 cycles) to the construct at a rate of 5%/sec.
Repeat the application of 10% cyclic strain until failure of the sample, incrementing by 10% cyclic strain for each subsequent test.
Drill a 4.5 mm diameter hole at the center of the ventilated cap of the reservoir tube without damaging the filter membrane that covers the aerating holes.
Press-fit a mandrel (diameter = 4.5 mm, length = 40 mm) into the hole and fix the mandrel as described in step 1.1.2.
Prepare two C-shaped silicone supports for the construct with an external diameter of 14 mm; internal diameter of 8 mm.
Position a rotating motor in one end of the rotating-wall bioreactor and a bearing on the other end.

Expand human umbilical vein endothelial cells (HUVECs) in 25 cm² culture flasks with 5 ml of M199 culture medium supplemented with 10% PS, 10% FBS, and 1% pen-strep in a Petri dish inside an incubator at T = 37 °C, 5% CO₂, and 100% humidity until 90% confluence.
Prepare 1.5 ml of the protein coating solution per construct by diluting the concentrate protein mixture to 10.5 ng/ml in serum-free endothelial cell culture medium.
Measure the length of the construct using a vernier caliper.

Calculate the luminal volume V and the luminal area A of the construct as: V = Din2 L/4 and A = Din L respectively (where Din is the inner diameter corresponding to the mandrel diameter, and L is the length of the construct).
Position the construct at the center of the reservoir following the harvesting procedure.
Use C-shaped silicone support to fix the construct at both ends to the reservoir.
Fill the reservoir with 35 ml of culture medium.
Fill 75% of the calculated luminal volume of the construct (V) with the protein coating solution prepared in step 4.2.2.
Close both extremities of the construct to avoid any leakage of the protein coating solution.
Assemble the rotating-wall bioreactor system inside the cell culture hood.
Place the bioreactor in a 37 °C incubator and start the rotation at 4.02 x 10-5 g force for 1 hour to allow luminal coating.
Open the upper extremity of the construct and aspirate the protein coating solution from the lumen.
Detach HUVECs (passage 2-3) by removing the culture medium from the flask of HUVECs and adding 3 ml of trypsin solution (1x in PBS).
Incubate for 5 minutes at 37 °C, 5% CO2, and 100% humidity.
Resuspend the HUVECs at a concentration of 4 x 106 cells/ml in supplemented M199 culture medium.
Seed HUVECs into the lumen of the construct with a density of 1,000 cells/cm² inside the cell culture hood.
Close the upper extremities of the construct to avoid leakage of the HUVECs solution.
Incubate the constructs in the rotating-wall bioreactor at T = 37 °C, 5% CO₂, and 100% humidity for 2 days.
Culture the constructs at a constant rotation of 4.02 x 10⁻⁵ g force.
Harvest the construct after 2 days of culture in sterile conditions.
Prepare the harvested construct for further biological characterization as described in section 2.4.
